% Pattern: head/case. A proof starts with a bold stage head right after its
% \begin, and a second stage follows. Each stage is a case of the proof, the
% first one too, since a proof has no head of its own to write again. Seen in
% the gold pilot (set X).
% want theorem-1 statement/theorem 1 status=here
% want proof-1 proof - proves=theorem-1
% want head-1 other/case A
% want head-2 other/case B
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{amsthm}
\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}
\begin{document}
\begin{theorem} Every regular cardinal is large. \end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
\textbf{Stage A:} We force by the initial segments of the tree.

\textbf{Stage B:} We show that the forcing is closed.
\end{proof}
\end{document}
